subject: Genetics
title: E. coli Long-Term Experiment
description: A 60-second lesson on E. coli Long-Term Experiment.

hook.text: In 1988, Richard Lenski started growing E. coli in flasks. He's still going—over 80,000 generations and counting.

buildup.text: Every day, the bacteria are transferred to fresh glucose.

discovery.text: After 31,500 generations, one lineage evolved to eat citrate—something E. coli normally can't do. A new trait emerged.

twist.text: Replaying from frozen ancestors showed the citrate ability needed multiple prior mutations to enable it.

climax.text: Lenski's experiment proved evolution is both predictable and contingent.

punchline.text: 80,000 generations in a flask. Evolution, bottled.

quiz.question: What new ability did E. coli evolve in Lenski's experiment?
